name: switch-cases
title: Switch on a state code, with a default
summary: A weather card that switches on an integer condition code: one eq block per case, a shared cloud drawn once for the range of cases 1–3, and a default case written as the two complementary blocks lt 0 and gt 3; rem commands label the cases in the document.
prompt: A current-weather card that shows a sun, cloud, rain or snow icon with its name and one line of advice, chosen from a condition code 0–3 (here 2, rain), and a "No data" state for any other code.
teaches: Write a switch as one conditionalOperations eq block per case value: only the matching block runs
Share drawing between several cases with a range block (ge 1 containing le 3) placed before the per-case blocks, like a fallthrough
Write the default case as the complement of all cases: here lt 0 plus gt 3, two blocks with the same content (there is no else and no or)
Label sections of a long command list with rem: a comment the document carries and players ignore
pitfalls: The Java parser knows only gt, ge, lt, le and eq: any other name, ne included (a json2rc extension), becomes 0, which is EQ, so a ne block silently runs when the values are equal, the opposite of what was meant
eq compares floats exactly: switch on whole-number codes, never on a computed fraction
A gap in the codes needs its own default block: with codes 0, 1 and 3, the default is lt 0, eq 2 and gt 3
Paint state carries across blocks: set colour and size at the top of every case, or a case inherits whatever the previous one set
A canvas laid out at fixed coordinates needs a fit rule: here one variable and a translate + scale at the top keep it centred and on screen at any size, without touching the cases

snippets.note: case 2: eq @condition 2, rain drops and text
range block for cases 1-3: the shared cloud
rem: a comment kept in the document

condition.meaning: 0 clear, 1 cloudy, 2 rain, 3 snow; anything else is no data

check.describe: condition 2: a cloud with three blue rain streaks, "Rain", "Take an umbrella.". 0 gives the yellow sun with eight rays, 1 the cloud alone, 3 the cloud with snow dots, -1 or 4 a grey "?" and "No data". Resized, the drawing is centred vertically (translate componentHeight() / 2 - 85) and shrinks below 300 dp wide (scale min(1, componentWidth() / 300)) so the longest line still fits: at 240 it is drawn at 0.8.
